title: Her day off: a regular asks 'is Angie in?' and the other advisor does each thing half
purpose: Story S5, a day slot 16 is off. A regular rings for Angie about work she told him to book. Josh is friendly and knows him, names a price before he knows what the truck needs, answers a doubt with 'it's all good stuff', asks when and offers a spot, and lets him go to 'I'll call her tomorrow'. This is what 'the shop sells less without her' sounds like.

mentioned.name: Angie Holloway
mentioned.role: off that day; the customer asks for her

call.day: the Monday of week T-6, a day slot 16 is off (rule R6; card S05, call 28)

scenario.who_calls: A regular of the Bonny Oaks shop, Roy Standifer, who deals with Angie.
scenario.job: transmission fluid service: an exchange, or a drain and fill
scenario.what_happens: Josh says she is off, knows the customer, puts him on hold to find the price of the fluid exchange and gives it. The customer says Angie mentioned something cheaper; Josh says both are good. Asked which he needs, Josh says he would do the exchange and asks when he wants to come in. The customer will call back when she is in; Josh says the price is the same either way, offers to hold a spot and is turned down.

facts.note: catalogue.json, class truck, standard parts: atf_exchange 450.42 (he says 'four-fifty'), atf_drain_fill 213.14 ('about half that'). The price he gives is right.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Josh.
Josh. Is Angie in?
She's off today. Back tomorrow. Anything I can help you with?
Well... this is Roy Standifer. She told me to call her about the transmission service on my truck.
Oh, hey, Mr. Standifer. The Sierra. Gotcha. Yeah, we can get you taken care of.
What's that run?
Uh, hang on one sec for me.
[on hold, 28 s: the hold message, then music]
Okay, thanks for holding. So the transmission fluid exchange on your Sierra, that's four-fifty.
Uh-huh.
Four-fifty. Angie said somethin' about a drain and fill bein' about half that.
Yeah, we've got that too. It's all good stuff, either way. We'll get you taken care of.
Well, which one do I need?
Uh — I mean, the exchange gets more of the old fluid out. I'd probably do that one. When were you wanting to come in?
I don't know. I think I'll just call back tomorrow when she's in. She knows the truck.
Gotcha. I mean, I can do everything she can. It's the same price either way.
I know it. No offense.
No, no.
None taken. Want me to put you down for something anyway? Hold you a spot?
Nah. I'll call her.
Alright, no worries. I'll tell her you called.
'Preciate it.
You bet.
